did: Took the hiss out of the owner's takes as part of the conditioning step home runs (#3607). The owner picked the chain by ear from CONVO-PD's A/B, "C2 is cleaner, go with C2": RNNoise on the raw take, HOST12's cut and level, then noisereduce's stationary gate, an expander and a trim. RNNoise runs through the render image's own ffmpeg, its model kept in the repo and pinned by its sum. The gate, expander and trim are ported to TypeScript and held to noisereduce's and numpy's own numbers, so home's image needs no Python. On the owner's five turns it matched the session-side C2 within 1 dB, and every word survived re-transcription. An earlier ffmpeg-only version was set aside when the owner chose C2.

calls.title: How C2 runs on home: port the gate to TypeScript rather than carry Python (C1610)
options: Python, numpy, scipy and noisereduce in the render image
A pure-ffmpeg chain, back to the owner as an A/B
RNNoise through ffmpeg and the gate, expander and trim ported to TypeScript
calls.why: noisereduce pulls about 250 MB into every pull of home's image, scipy and matplotlib among it, for a gate of about 200 lines; the port matches it within 1e-7 on a fixture and within 1 dB on the owner's take.
calls.undo: Put Python and noisereduce in infra/render/Dockerfile and run the gate there instead of spectralGate and expand, as a call that moves C1610.

left: Nothing on home runs it yet: conditionTake has no caller on main until HOST13's record-to-video bridge (#3555) calls it with rnnoiseModel(), as noted there.
C1611, the owner's C2, has no options or why-gray of its own: those are the owner's to give.
